title: Making distant LOD (object LOD) for a static object in Fallout 4
content:
Making distant LOD (object LOD) for a static object in Fallout 4
Distant LOD meshes are separate NIF files, one per level, named <Name>_LOD_0.nif, <Name>_LOD_1.nif, <Name>_LOD_2.nif and kept under Meshes\LOD\ (for example Meshes\LOD\Architecture\Shacks\). Vanilla keeps their textures under Textures\LOD\ and their materials under Materials\LOD\, small and separate from the full-detail textures.
Keep them very low: across 900 vanilla LOD meshes the median _LOD_0 is 8 triangles, 90% are 125 or fewer, the largest is about 2,200 (the USS Constitution), and city buildings use roughly 150-450.
A LOD material must not point at the full-size textures: if the LOD NIF still names the object's own .bgsm, the game draws the 4K textures on every LOD, because the .bgsm overrides the textures in the NIF.
Attaching them (do NOT make a separate STAT for a LOD mesh):
1. Open the object's own STAT record, the one with the full-detail model that you place in the world.
2. Tick Has Distant LOD, click Specify distant LOD meshes..., and set level 0, 1 and 2 to the _LOD_0/1/2 meshes.
3. Generate object LOD for the worldspace (in the Creation Kit or with xLODGen). The game only shows LOD from that generated data.
If you copy a vanilla LOD STAT (for example CambridgeBuilding05_LOD) and point it at your LOD mesh, the preview stays empty: those records have Is Marker ticked, and markers are not drawn.
Flat billboard LODs (_LOD_FLAT) are for trees: only two vanilla meshes use one, both maple trees. Buildings and props use real LOD meshes.

title: Why LODs made by decimating fall apart on plants and buildings made of many pieces
content:
Why LODs made by decimating fall apart on plants and buildings made of many pieces
Decimate removes triangles piece by piece. A model made of hundreds of thin separate pieces (tendrils, leaves, spikes, a building overgrown with plant meshes) breaks into floating shards at LOD triangle counts, and its silhouette disappears.
A better LOD for such models is one solid simplified skin: voxel-remesh the whole model, drop tiny loose bits, decimate that skin to the target count, UV-unwrap it and bake the original's colour and normal maps onto it. Measured on a 7,700-triangle overgrown house (outline overlap with the original from 12 views): solid skin 0.83 / 0.83 / 0.87 at 1,500 / 500 / 150 triangles, decimation 0.81 / 0.61 / 0.08.
The Mossy Blender add-on 5.4.5 does this by default (LOD generator, method Solid Shell): it writes _LOD_0/1/2 NIFs with their own baked textures (1K / 512 / 256) and .bgsm files under Meshes\LOD, Textures\LOD and Materials\LOD. Set its output folder to the mod's root folder (the one that holds Meshes and Textures); a folder inside the mod is cut back to the root automatically. Versions before 5.4.5 decimated, kept the full-size material and saved PNG textures the game cannot load.

title: Textures come out darker after converting PNG/TGA to DDS with texconv (use -srgb)
content:
Textures come out darker after converting PNG/TGA to DDS with texconv (use -srgb)
texconv treats a PNG or TGA as sRGB and, when writing a normal (UNORM) DDS format, converts it to linear. The result is visibly darker, and normal maps get distorted. Measured: a diffuse averaging 0.168 came out at 0.050; a normal map pixel (0.25, 0.5) came out at (0.05, 0.22).
Fix: add -srgb to the texconv command (texconv -y -f BC7_UNORM -srgb -o <folder> <file>). It keeps the values as they are, and the output format stays the same (DXT1, DXT5, BC5 and BC7_UNORM were checked). Converting DDS back to PNG is not affected.
The Mossy Blender add-on before 5.4.5 converted without -srgb, so textures it converted from PNG/TGA may be too dark and their normal maps off; convert or export them again with 5.4.5.

title: Leaf cards and see-through plant parts: alpha cutout and two-sided in the NIF, the .bgsm and Blender
content:
Leaf cards and see-through plant parts: alpha cutout and two-sided in the NIF, the .bgsm and Blender
A leaf card is a flat mesh whose diffuse texture's alpha channel cuts out the leaf shape. It needs the cutout and two-sided set in both places the game reads:
- In the NIF: a NiAlphaProperty with alpha test on (vanilla uses flags 4844 with a threshold around 127-128), and the shader's DOUBLE_SIDED flag.
- In the .bgsm: alpha test on with its threshold, and two-sided on. The .bgsm overrides the NIF, so if it has alpha test off the cutout does not show.
In Blender with PyNifly, a mesh loaded from a NIF uses PyNifly's own 'Fallout 4 MTS' shader group: textures are image nodes named Diffuse_Texture, Normal_Texture, Specular_Texture and Glow_Map_Texture feeding its Diffuse, Normal, Smooth Spec and Glow Map inputs. The cutout is the 'Alpha Property' node (Alpha Test on/off, Alpha Threshold 0-255), and PyNifly writes the NiAlphaProperty from it on export. The .bgsm path is the material property BSLSP_Shader_Name, and the shader flags are the Shader_Flags_1 / Shader_Flags_2 properties. Don't plug a Principled BSDF into such a material's output: that disconnects the NIF shader and its textures.
The Mossy Blender add-on 5.4.5's 'Set Up as Leaf Card' keeps the mesh's textures and material and adds all of this, including switching on alpha test and two-sided in the existing .bgsm (the original is kept as .bgsm.bak; game files are never edited).

title: Creation Kit crashes from Blender-exported collision (empty compressed mesh, 'Instance should have already been created')
content:
Creation Kit crashes from Blender-exported collision (empty compressed mesh, 'Instance should have already been created')
Two collision exports crash the Creation Kit:
1. Exact-mesh / building collision written by PyNifly (v27 and v28) as hknpCompressedMeshShape: PyNifly leaves the shape's search tree empty at every size, while all 167,285 vanilla compressed meshes have it filled. The CK crashes inside the Havok loader. Exporting that collision as a convex hull (up to 128 vertices) instead loads fine.
2. A building whose collision pieces are all bodies of one bhkPhysicsSystem, as PyNifly writes it: placing it crashes with 'Instance should have already been created' (bhknpcollisionobject.cpp line 611), because Havok rejects the physics data and the system ends up with no instance. Giving each piece its own single-body bhkPhysicsSystem loads fine; vanilla precombined meshes carry up to 590 such systems.
The Mossy Blender add-on 5.4.4 fixed the first and 5.4.5 the second. Plain vanilla facts for reference: collision objects use flags 128, and BSXFlags 0x82 is the usual value for plants with collision.
If the crash continues after re-exporting, check that the Creation Kit is not still reading an older copy of the NIF from another mod in Mod Organizer.

title: Walking through plants that were given collision in Blender (plants merged into a cliff or rock that already has collision)
content:
Walking through plants that were given collision in Blender (plants merged into a cliff or rock that already has collision)
Symptom: plants added to a bigger model (for example fungus plants merged into a cliff NIF) were given collision in the Mossy Blender add-on, but in game the player walks straight through them, while the same plants exported on their own do block the player.
Cause 1 (fixed in add-on 5.5.2): the model's root node already had Havok collision (the cliff's own compressed mesh). After export the add-on attaches convex-hull collision itself, and before 5.5.2 it skipped that step whenever the root already had collision, so only the cliff's collision reached the file. Check it in NifSkope: a plant with working collision has its own NiNode with a bhkNPCollisionObject and its own bhkPhysicsSystem. If the plants have none, the file has no collision for them.
Cause 2 (also fixed in 5.5.2): when several plants are one mesh object, a single convex hull around all of them fills the empty space between the plants with an invisible wall. The add-on now gives a mesh made of separate pieces one hull per plant: a small piece (a cap, a leaf) joins a bigger piece only when at least half of its bounding box is inside that piece, and there are at most 32 pieces per mesh.
How the fixed file is laid out (the same layout vanilla uses for several collision objects in one NIF): the existing collision stays where it is, and every new piece gets its own NiNode under the root with a bhkNPCollisionObject (flags 128, body 0) and its own single-body bhkPhysicsSystem. One physics system per piece is required; several bodies in one system crash the Creation Kit.
Fix: update the add-on to 5.5.2, select the plant mesh, run Add Collision again, then export the whole model again (all pieces as one NIF). Make sure the new NIF is the one the game loads (no older copy winning in Mod Organizer's left pane), and keep BSXFlags with the Havok bit (2) set: the cliff's own collision already sets it.
Plants with collision that sit in their own NIF already worked before 5.5.2, because there the root had no collision of its own.

title: Collision made in Blender sits beside the model instead of on it (tree or plant inside an imported NIF)
content:
Collision made in Blender sits beside the model instead of on it (tree or plant inside an imported NIF)
Symptom: after Add Collision or Custom Collision on one piece of an imported model (for example a fungus tree that is part of a cliff NIF), the UCX_ collision object appears off to the side, lower or turned compared to the mesh, and in game the collision is somewhere other than the tree.
Cause: imported NIFs keep their node tree in Blender, so a mesh can sit under parent nodes that are moved and rotated (here a node turned 63 degrees). The Mossy Blender add-on's collision tools parented the new collision so that it kept only the mesh's own local offset and lost every transform above it; the collision ended up about 600 units to the side and 560 units down. Meshes directly under the root were not affected, because there that chain does nothing.
Fix: add-on 5.5.2 keeps the collision exactly on the mesh whatever its parent nodes do (all collision tools: Add Collision, Custom Collision, collision from LOD, compound and multi-piece). Delete the misplaced UCX_ object and generate the collision again. Check: the UCX_ wireframe must wrap the mesh in the viewport; after export the hull's position in the NIF must match the shape's.
Tip for trees and mushroom clusters: Add Collision gives each separate plant its own convex hull; Custom (exact mesh) collision is exported as one convex hull around everything, which covers the gaps between separate mushrooms.

title: Cliff or rock texture suddenly looks like one big stretched texture, grass looks wrong after re-exporting from Blender (UVs were repacked into 0-1)
content:
Cliff or rock texture suddenly looks like one big stretched texture, grass looks wrong after re-exporting from Blender (UVs were repacked into 0-1)
Symptom: after a re-export from Blender, a cliff, rock or ground piece shows its texture once, stretched over the whole model instead of repeating, and grass or plant cards show the wrong parts of their texture. Nothing changed in the BGSM or the DDS files.
Cause: the mesh's UV map was rebuilt. Landscape pieces tile their texture with UVs far outside 0-1 (a vanilla-style cliff piece ran from about -4 to +5), and grass cards also reach past the square (-0.17 to 1.22). Any UV tool that unwraps or packs islands (Smart UV Project, Pack Islands, Re-Unwrap, Lightmap Pack) squeezes every island into one 0-1 square, so the texture stops tiling and the cards point at the wrong spots. A rebuilt unwrap also adds UV seams, so the exported shape has more vertices than before (220 -> 268 on one cliff piece, 562 -> 605 on a grass card) while the triangles stay the same.
How to check: in NifSkope or Blender's UV editor compare the shape's UVs with the original NIF. Tiling UVs well outside 0-1 that are now all inside 0-1 means the unwrap was replaced.
Fix: never run Pack Islands / Re-Unwrap / Smart UV Project on tiling landscape pieces or grass. If it already happened, re-import the original NIF (or a backup) and redo the edits, or copy the old UVs back: when the triangles did not change, every triangle can be matched to the original by its corner positions and its UVs restored exactly. Do the restore in Blender too (re-import the fixed NIF), otherwise the next export from the same scene brings the broken UVs back.
Most common cause, found later the same day: one mesh in the export had no UV map. The exporter made a placeholder UV map with Edit Mode + Smart UV Project while the rest of the model was selected, and Blender's multi-object Edit Mode re-unwrapped every selected mesh. The exported NIF got squeezed UVs on most shapes (8 of 12 in a test) while the Blender scene still looked right, so the problem only showed in game. Fixed in the Mossy add-on 5.5.2: only the mesh without UVs is unwrapped. Same trap by hand: never run Smart UV Project or Unwrap with several objects in Edit Mode unless all of them should be unwrapped.
Also seen: a solid cliff body on an alpha-blended decal material (an '8Bit' BGSM) only looked solid while its texture had no alpha; once the texture's vanilla alpha was back it turned see-through. Solid parts need an opaque material (blending, alpha test and decal off); only the fading decal pieces use the blended one.
A mesh that shows black in Blender has usually lost its UV map. The Mossy add-on (5.5.2) now gives such a mesh its original UVs back on export, matched triangle by triangle from the game's copy of the NIF or the NIF it was imported from, and says so in the export message; only when the mesh was changed too much does it fall back to a placeholder unwrap, with a warning that the texture will not line up.

title: Hard straight edges where a cliff or mound meets the ground: the decal pieces' fade is ignored because their material does not blend
content:
Hard straight edges where a cliff or mound meets the ground: the decal pieces' fade is ignored because their material does not blend
Symptom: at the foot of a dirt cliff or mud mound you see dark slabs with straight, sharp edges lying on the ground instead of patches that fade into the terrain. Retexturing the ground (even with seam fixes) does not help.
How vanilla blends these models: besides the mound itself, the NIF has flat decal pieces lying on the ground (for example GSDirtCliffLarge01 has Object007:1 with GlowingSeaCorrosion01_Alpha.BGSM and Object007:15 with GlowingSeaRubble01Decal8Bit.BGSM). Their edges fade out through vertex alpha (128 of 220 and 37 of 51 vertices below full alpha), the NIF has a blending NiAlphaProperty (flags 0x10ED and 0x12ED, threshold 128), the Decal shader flag is set, and the BGSM has alpha blending on (mode Standard, blend 6/7), Decal and Decal No Fade on; the Rubble one also uses alpha test 128.
Cause: a retexture mod pointed those decal pieces at an opaque material (a cliff or ground BGSM with alpha blending and alpha test off). The game uses the BGSM's alpha settings, so the vertex-alpha fade in the mesh is ignored and every patch is drawn solid.
Fix: keep the texture but give the decal pieces their own copy of the material with the vanilla decal settings: alpha blend on (Standard, 6/7), Decal and Decal No Fade on, alpha test on with 128 only for the 8-bit rubble style piece. Point only the decal shapes at the copy (for example GSMuckCliff02_Decal.bgsm), never change the shared material in place, because the cliff body uses it opaque. Set the Decal shader flag on those shapes in the NIF too.
How to find them: look for shapes that have vertex colors with alpha near 0 and a NiAlphaProperty with blending, but whose BGSM has blending and alpha test both off.

title: Glowing plant does not show in game after a Blender export; it comes back when the NIF Emissive Color is set to black
content:
Glowing plant does not show in game after a Blender export; it comes back when the NIF Emissive Color is set to black
Symptom: a glowing plant or mushroom that uses a BGSM (Glow Map and Own Emit on) stops showing in game after it was exported from Blender. In NifSkope its BSLightingShaderProperty has a coloured Emissive Color (the BGSM's glow colour, for example #a953ff); setting Emissive Color back to 0,0,0 makes it show again.
Cause: when PyNifly imports a NIF it reads the BGSM and fills the Blender material's emission tint from the BGSM's Emittance colour. Exporters that copy that tint back into the NIF write the BGSM colour into the NIF's Emissive Color, while the original file had black. Tested in game: the coloured version did not show, the black version did.
Rule: when a shape uses a BGSM, the glow belongs in the BGSM (Emit Enabled, Emittance colour, Glow Map) and the NIF's Emissive Color can stay black. That is a normal vanilla layout: 596 vanilla glow-map shapes with a BGSM have black there. Shapes with no material file keep their NIF colour, because there the NIF is the material.
Fix: the Mossy Blender add-on (5.5.2) now writes black Emissive Color on every shape that uses a BGSM or BGEM, on every export, so it no longer has to be fixed by hand in NifSkope. For files already exported, set Emissive Color to 0,0,0 in NifSkope on those shapes; leave the BGSM's glow settings as they are.

title: Plant disappears in Blender (only the selection outline is left) right after clicking Wind
content:
Plant disappears in Blender (only the selection outline is left) right after clicking Wind
Symptom: a plant imported from a NIF looks fine in Blender until Wind is applied; then its textured surface vanishes from the viewport and only the orange selection outline is left. Nothing is wrong with the mesh or the textures.
Cause: Wind stores the sway amount in the mesh's vertex alpha (the VERTEX_ALPHA colour attribute PyNifly exports as vertex alpha): 0 at the base, rising toward the tips. With the BGSM's Tree flag on, Fallout 4 reads vertex alpha as sway. But the Blender material PyNifly built on import still feeds VERTEX_ALPHA into its AlphaProperty node as transparency with an alpha cutoff of about 0.5, so every part that sways less than half is cut away in the viewport. PyNifly itself leaves that link out when it imports a tree material, for the same reason.
Fix: the Mossy Blender add-on (5.5.2) takes the Vertex Alpha link out of the material preview when Wind is applied and puts it back when wind is removed. Only the viewport changes: the exported NIF is byte-identical with or without the link. By hand: in the Shader Editor, remove the link from the 'Vertex Alpha' attribute node into the AlphaProperty node's 'Vertex Alpha' input.
Related: in game the same sway values show up as transparency (half the plant invisible) when the material's Tree flag is off, so wind plants need a BGSM with Tree on.

title: Part of the model is missing after exporting a plant from Blender (custom mesh added next to the original game mesh)
content:
Part of the model is missing after exporting a plant from Blender (custom mesh added next to the original game mesh)
Symptom: you import a plant NIF, add your own mesh (for example extra leaf cards) next to the original game mesh, give your mesh wind and export. In game or NifSkope only your mesh is there; the original stock is gone.
Cause: exporting the selected object writes a NIF with just that object. The other shapes the imported NIF had (here the original stock, a BSMeshLODTriShape with its LOD levels) are left out, and saving over the original file loses them.
Fix: the Mossy Blender add-on (5.5.2) exports the whole model when the selected mesh sits under an imported NIF root next to other visible meshes, and says which pieces it included; hidden pieces stay out and are named. With an older add-on, select every piece of the model (or use the export that combines the selected meshes) before exporting.
Wind on only one piece: only the meshes that sway should get the Tree_Anim shader flag and a Tree material; vanilla wind NIFs (BSLeafAnimNode root) leave non-swaying parts without Tree_Anim (397 such shaders). The add-on now sets Tree_Anim only on the wind meshes' materials, so the original stock keeps its own material and does not sway.
Note: External Emittance in a BGSM is copied into the NIF's Shader Flags 1 (bit 29) by the exporter. No vanilla landscape material (0 of 485) uses it; if it is on in a plant's BGSM, that is the material's own setting.
Texture paths in the NIF: vanilla NIF texture sets write 'Textures\Landscape\Plants\X_d.dds' (raw scan of 1,709 vanilla landscape NIFs: 7,284 paths with the Textures\ prefix, none with forward slashes). BGSMs write 'Landscape/Plants/X_d.dds'. If one slot of a NIF texture set (often the glow map) shows the BGSM form, change it to the NIF form; the add-on (5.5.2) now does this on export.

title: Blender error "'NoneType' object has no attribute 'collision_type'" (or 'slot', 'preset') in the Mossy add-on's panels
content:
Blender error "'NoneType' object has no attribute 'collision_type'" (or 'slot', 'preset') in the Mossy add-on's panels
Older versions of the Mossy Blender add-on (before 5.4.5) could print errors like AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'collision_type' from ui_panels.py in Blender's console, and a panel (for example LOD & Collision) failed to draw.
Cause: many of the add-on's tools register about 3 seconds after Blender starts (or on the first change to the scene). Until then Blender hands the panel nothing for those buttons, and the panel crashed setting an option on them. It is harmless: the error stops once those tools have loaded. If it keeps repeating long after start-up, the delayed tools failed to load; check Blender's system console (Window > Toggle System Console) for messages after 'Phase 2'.
Version 5.4.5 fixes it: the buttons always draw and get their options once the tools exist.

title: Mossy Blender add-on: tools add to a mesh's textures and materials, never replace them (5.4.5)
content:
Mossy Blender add-on: tools add to a mesh's textures and materials, never replace them (5.4.5)
Since version 5.4.5 every tool in the Mossy Blender add-on that touches a material only adds to what the mesh already has: material setup, Install Texture, Auto-Connect Textures, applying a .bgsm, Material Browser presets, Setup HD Material, Set Up as Leaf Card, joining meshes / Combine Vegetation, Apply Displacement and image import. Existing texture files are never written over when textures are copied or converted.
Older versions could, mostly on meshes loaded from a NIF: swap the material for an empty one, plug a new shader into the material output (the original textures were still in the node tree but no longer connected), delete the other materials after a join, turn leaves one-sided when a .bgsm was applied, or write over an existing .dds. If an older version removed your textures from a mesh (they vanished after using one of those tools), you can usually get them back: open the Shader Editor, where the original image nodes (Diffuse_Texture etc.) are often still there and can be reconnected, or reload the NIF.
Also fixed in 5.4.5: exporting had not created any new .bgsm files since 5.4.0 (existing ones were kept, new materials never got one).
Tools whose job is to put a new texture in a slot still do so when asked: Install Texture with a file you pick, Generate + Apply Texture, Wrap Image, baking AO into the diffuse, and picking a glow map. 'Mark as Collision Mesh' still clears that mesh's materials, as collision needs none.

title: A tree whose leaves are part of the trunk mesh (AI-made or baked tree): collision and wind in Fallout 4
content:
A tree whose leaves are part of the trunk mesh (AI-made or baked tree): collision and wind in Fallout 4
Many AI-generated or baked trees are ONE mesh with ONE material: the trunk, branches and leaves are joined. Tools that split by loose parts or by material then see a single piece, which causes two problems:
- Collision: one convex hull around the whole tree, so the player bumps into an invisible wall around the leaves. Vanilla trees do not do that. Measured on the unpacked game: BlastedForestFungalTreeLarge01 has about 9 separate convex pieces along the trunk, root flare and crown masses, smaller than the visible tree (794 x 747 units against 1118 x 1238); BlastedForestBurntTreeUpright01 has one tight piece around the trunk (154 x 195 against 288 x 366). Leaves get no collision.
- Wind: painting the wind by height (or along the whole piece) makes the trunk sway as much as the leaves. Vanilla trees with wind that are one shape (TreeElmForest01, TreeElmFree01, TreeMapleInstitute01Green) keep the bottom 20% at 0 and paint by distance from the trunk: 0.03-0.06 next to the trunk even high up, about 0.2-0.4 a little way out, up to 0.9-1.0 at the outer canopy. Trees made of separate shapes (TreeMapleForest1) put the trunk in a material without the Tree (wind) flag, so it never moves. The Glowing Sea trees TreeGS01/02 and the blasted trees have no wind at all.
You do not have to separate the leaves from the trunk. The Mossy Fallout 4 Blender add-on (5.5.2 and later) finds the solid woody parts itself: a face belongs to the trunk when a ray shot inward travels at least 3% of the tree's height before leaving the same solid (leaves are thin shells or flat cards).
- Add Collision, or Add Custom Collision on a tree that is too detailed for an exact mesh, then builds several compact convex hulls around the trunk, thick branches and root flare; the leaves get none. On a test tree: 5 hulls, about 27 times less volume than one hull over everything, 1% of leaf faces inside a hull. It exports as separate convex pieces with one physics system each.
- Wind with type Tree paints a one-piece tree by distance from the trunk surface at each height times height above the base, then evens out any edge where the weight would jump, so nothing stretches. On the test tree the trunk went from 0.28-0.91 to 0.00-0.06 while the leaves still move (up to about 0.9). Re-painted vanilla one-piece trees came out closer to Bethesda's own values than the older painting (38.7 against 43.5 of 255 average difference).
After changing a tree: redo the collision and the wind (Wind button), then export. A separate trunk and leaf mesh still works too and keeps the older per-piece painting.

title: Tree or plant partly invisible in game (trunk or bottom missing, leaves floating) after adding wind
content:
Tree or plant partly invisible in game (trunk or bottom missing, leaves floating) after adding wind
Cause: the wind weights are stored in the vertex colour ALPHA (0 = still, 1 = full sway). Fallout 4 reads that alpha as sway only when the material (.bgsm) has the Tree flag on. With Tree off the same alpha is transparency: the game multiplies it into the texture alpha, and with alpha test on every pixel under the cut disappears. The still parts of a wind mesh (trunk, base) have alpha near 0, so exactly they vanish while the canopy stays.
Seen in game on a one-piece AI tree: wind painted, NIF shader had Tree_Anim on, but its .bgsm had Tree off and alpha test 127: 6,260 of 15,500 vertices were under the cut, the whole lower trunk (alpha 0.00-0.12) was gone.
The game uses the .bgsm, not the NIF's own shader flags: in all 224,214 vanilla NIFs (1,099,964 shape/material pairs) the NIF says Tree_Anim on with the material Tree off only 2 times (Thistle01), and the reverse (NIF off, material on) 3,416 times, which sways normally.
Fix: turn Tree on in the material. If that .bgsm is shared with other meshes, give the wind mesh its own copy (for example GSFungusStock04B_Wind.bgsm) instead: a shared mesh whose vertex alpha is 1.0 everywhere would otherwise sway completely, base included. Vanilla also uses vertex alpha as deliberate transparency on non-wind meshes (hairlines, Diamond City edge trims; Thistle01's picked state hides 427 of 437 vertices that way, with the NIF's Vertex_Alpha flag on), so low vertex alpha alone is not an error.
The Blender add-on now reports this in Check Against Game (a mesh with a Wind group, low vertex alpha and a Tree-off material) and after export (wind NIF + Tree-off material + alpha under the cut = ERROR, parts INVISIBLE).
Related: no vanilla .bgsm (0 of 8,279) starts a texture path with Textures\; write Landscape\Trees\X_d.dds, not Textures\Landscape\Trees\X_d.dds. Same symptom from the add-on's Tree Tools (Leaf Cards / Tree Wind: Wood Still, Cards Sway), 2026-11-17 on a rose-like fungus tree: those two buttons wrote the wind into vertex alpha but did not mark the material as a Tree material the way the general wind button does, so the export saw no wind (no BSLeafAnimNode root, no Tree_Anim) and kept the shared .bgsm with Tree off - the still bark (alpha 0) was cut away in game while it still showed in Blender. Fixed in the add-on: Tree Tools now marks it, and the export gives the plant its own <name>_Wind.bgsm with Tree on (a shared material with Tree off - used by an ash mound and the tree's LODs - is left alone). For a one-piece tree with a bud on top and hanging leaves, good wind is: trunk 0; the neck ramping smoothly to a gentle value at the top of the bud (about 0.35), the same all round so the bud sways as one; every hanging strip starting at the value where it hangs and ramping to about 0.6-0.75 at its tip.
Related, all BLACK in game instead of invisible: a plant that had no vertex colours before gets them when wind is added; if only the wind layer (VERTEX_ALPHA) was set, the red/green/blue part is written as 0,0,0 and the game multiplies the texture by it, so the plant shows black. Fix: a white colour layer (Col, 1,1,1) next to VERTEX_ALPHA, or set the colour bytes to 255,255,255 and keep the alpha. The add-on adds the white layer itself since 2026-11-17 (GSFungusTree10: 1,948 vertices were 0,0,0).

title: NIF shader flags versus the .bgsm material: which one Fallout 4 uses
content:
NIF shader flags versus the .bgsm material: which one Fallout 4 uses
When a BSLightingShaderProperty names a .bgsm, the game uses the material file's settings; the shader flags stored in the NIF are a leftover copy that vanilla often lets drift. Raw count over all 224,214 vanilla NIFs (1,099,964 shape/material pairs), NIF on + .bgsm off / NIF off + .bgsm on:
Cast shadows 574 / 25,839; Environment mapping 241 / 9,051; Hair 8,399 / 379; Decal 1,122 / 4,539; Greyscale to palette 45 / 2,581; Glow map 33 / 1,982; Two-sided 193 / 1,874; Tree (wind) 2 / 3,416; Skin tint 0 / 41; Z-buffer write 10 / 0.
So a difference between NifSkope's shader flags and the material is normal and harmless, except where it shows a real conflict: wind (Tree_Anim) on in the NIF with Tree off in the material means the mesh will not sway, and its wind alpha becomes transparency (see the invisible-tree entry). Change behaviour in the .bgsm (Material Editor), not only in NifSkope's flags.
Note for tool makers: PyNifly fills a shader's flags from its .bgsm when it finds one, so reading flags through PyNifly compares the material with itself; read the NIF bytes to see what the file really says.

content:
A new mesh exported from Blender shows Flags 0 on its BSTriShape in NifSkope
PyNifly writes a shape's NiAVObject Flags only when the Blender object still carries the flags from an imported NIF; a mesh made in Blender (AI-generated, sculpted, baked) is written with Flags 0. title: Wind on a one-piece tree: thick parts (crown, solid prongs, thick limbs) should stay still, only branches and leaves sway
content:
Wind on a one-piece tree: thick parts (crown, solid prongs, thick limbs) should stay still, only branches and leaves sway
Painting wind by distance from the trunk keeps the trunk still, but solid wood that sticks out (a wide crown, finger-like prongs, thick limbs) is also far from the trunk and was painted to sway like leaves. On a fungal test tree the crown prongs (1.1-2.3% of the tree height thick) got up to full sway.
What tells a prong from a branch is the path from the trunk: a branch turns thin a short way out and stays thin to its leaves (canopy median 0.55% of the height), a prong stays thick to its tip. The Blender add-on's Wind (type Tree) now limits the sway by how much THIN material (under about 1-2% of the height thick) lies between a vertex and the solid trunk, measured along the mesh: crown and thick prongs 0.16 -> 0.07 on average, canopy unchanged (0.88 -> 0.87), branches stiff at the trunk and freer toward the tips. Very thin tendrils on top may still move a little, which looks natural.
Trade-off, stated honestly: against Bethesda's own painting on four vanilla one-piece trees the average difference went from 38.2 to 41.4 of 255, because Bethesda lets thick limbs move somewhat.
A tree imported from a NIF is split at every UV seam; the add-on now counts vertices at the same spot as connected, so such a tree still gets the one-piece tree painting instead of the height ramp (which makes the top sway).

title: LODs for a tree with leaves in Fallout 4: how vanilla builds them, and why decimating the tree fails
content:
LODs for a tree with leaves in Fallout 4: how vanilla builds them, and why decimating the tree fails
Measured on Bethesda's pre-war trees (Meshes\LOD\Landscape\Trees\Chargen: TreeMaplePW01Gr, TreeElmFreePW01Gr, TreeElmFrstPW01Gr, TreeMaplePW03Gr against their full trees):
- _LOD_0 and _LOD_1 are TWO shapes. The trunk is one closed low-poly piece: 50-158 triangles at _LOD_0, 25-53 at _LOD_1, opaque one-sided material (Materials\LOD\PreWarTreeTrunksLOD.BGSM, 512px DXT1). The canopy is separate leaf cards: 17-65 cards at _LOD_0, 13-31 at _LOD_1, about 2-3 triangles each, mostly tilted or upright (only 0-28% flat), card size about a quarter of the tree height, one material shared by both levels (alpha test 90-105, two-sided, 512px DXT5 + BC5 normal) and an NiAlphaProperty (flags 4844).
- _LOD_2 is a crossed billboard: two crossed quads, 8 vertices, 4 triangles, a picture of the whole tree (256px DXT5, alpha test 100-127).
Decimating a leafy tree instead cuts the leaves into loose triangles with no solid trunk under them: a one-piece AI tree came out with 77% / 85% / 90% open edges at its three levels and looked shattered.
Textures: vanilla does NOT bake new pictures for _LOD_0 and _LOD_1. All 54 Chargen pre-war tree LODs use Textures\LOD\PreWarTreeTrunksLOD (the bark strip, shrunk to 512) for the trunk shape and PreWarMapleGrLOD / PreWarElmGrLOD (the leaf-branch picture from the full tree's 2048x4096 atlas, shrunk to 512) for the canopy shape; only _LOD_2 (lv2) is a rendered picture of the whole tree. That is why they look sharp: the LOD shows the real texture, just smaller.
The Blender add-on's Generate LODs has 'Tree: Trunk + Leaf Cards (like vanilla)' and picks it for trees (wind or collision type Tree, 'tree' in the name, or a model/material under a Trees folder). For a tree that has leaf cards (a card material: many small flat pieces) it builds the LODs the vanilla way: the real trunk reduced but keeping its own UVs and bark texture (the smallest reduction whose surface stays within 0.4% / 0.6% of the tree height; a Glowing Sea tree gave 961 and 719 triangles, while 6% or less broke it into spikes), plus a selection of the tree's own leaf cards (80 / 40, spread over the crown and grown about where they meet the twig so the canopy keeps its leaf area), all on the tree's own textures shrunk to the LOD Texture Size (512 by default: _d BC3, _n and _s BC5) with Materials\LOD\<folder>\<Name>LOD.bgsm shared by both levels; _LOD_2 is a crossed billboard picture. Card sets under 5% of the card area (small bits at the roots) are left out. A tree whose leaves are part of the trunk mesh gets rendered cards and a baked trunk instead; run Tree Tools > Replace Leaves with Leaf Cards first to get the vanilla-style result.
LOD meshes only appear if the plugin points at them: the STAT record needs the Has Distant LOD flag and its MNAM LOD paths (for example LOD\Landscape\Trees\GlowingSea\MyTree_LOD_0.nif ... _LOD_2.nif), and the object LOD has to be generated again with xLODGen afterwards. Check that every MNAM path matches a real file name; a renamed LOD file silently leaves that object without LOD.

title: Fallout 4 collision you can walk through from some sides: collision on a scaled node
content:
Fallout 4 collision you can walk through from some sides: collision on a scaled node
Symptom: a tree's collision stops you from one side but you walk through it from the sides and back, while the collision looks right in Blender or NifSkope.
Cause found on a Glowing Sea tree: its four convex hulls sat on child NiNodes with scale 7.4 (the scale of the object they were made from). Of 14,604 collision nodes in the vanilla game meshes (Landscape, SetDressing, Architecture, DLC03, DLC04) only ONE has a scale other than 1, and it is a root node (TreeElmFreePreWar01Green, 1.2). Bethesda never relies on a child node's scale for collision.
Fix: bake the scale into the hull points (multiply every point, and the body position, by the scale) and set the node scale to 1. The collision is then the same shape whether or not the engine applies the node scale. Keep the convex radius as it was (vanilla tree hulls 0.001-0.01). Vanilla trees with convex collision use the Havok material Wood (24 of 24).
The Mossy Blender add-on now does this automatically after every export and reports 'collision node scale baked into the hull'.

title: Fallout 4 plant wind: a flower head, bulb or fruit sitting on another piece must move as one value
content:
Fallout 4 plant wind: a flower head, bulb or fruit sitting on another piece must move as one value
Symptom: the top of a plant (a bulb in a cone on a stalk) stretches and wobbles apart in the wind.
Cause: each separate piece was painted from 0 at its own bottom to the full value at its top, so a bulb went from 0 to 186 (of 255) inside itself while the cone under it was already at 164 where they meet. The tree wind shader sets both how far AND when a vertex sways from its alpha, so different values inside one solid piece stretch it, and different values where two pieces meet pull them apart.
What Bethesda does (207 vanilla tree and plant NIFs): a compact piece resting on a moving piece is one value (77%) equal to the supporting piece's value where they meet (88% within 25 of 255); pieces in general start where their support is (88%), and flat leaf cards sit at or above their support (89%).
The Mossy Blender add-on's Vegetation Wind now gives a compact piece that rests on another piece one value: the value of what it rests on, preferring a compact support (a bulb follows its cup, not a leaf beside it). Long pieces (leaves, branches) are still painted from 0 along their length: starting them at their support's value moved the painting further from Bethesda's own values (17 of 23 vanilla shapes worse), so that part was not adopted.
Also tested and NOT made the default: giving every leaf blade of a one-piece tree one value. On Bethesda's one-piece trees it moved the painting away from their own values (41.4 -> 45.4 of 255): their leaves do vary.

title: Fallout 4 NIF layout: BSXFlags and the wind node (BSLeafAnimNode) belong on the root only
content:
Fallout 4 NIF layout: BSXFlags and the wind node (BSLeafAnimNode) belong on the root only
Scan of 17,153 vanilla meshes (Landscape, SetDressing, Architecture and all DLC): BSXFlags on any node other than the root: 0. A BSLeafAnimNode anywhere but the root: 0. Collision on a scaled child node: 1 of 14,604 collision nodes, and that one is a root. Collision under a wind node (51 meshes) and collision nodes inside other collision nodes (436) are normal.
Two mod meshes broke these rules. A tree re-exported from Blender came out with an extra node level: a wind root, then an inner node holding the BSXFlags and the main collision. In game the player walked through it from some sides. An ash mound built by pasting several meshes into one file had 3 BSXFlags on inner nodes, 4 nested wind nodes, collision on nodes scaled 7.4, and two identical copies of the same tree stacked in the same place (one without wind colours, so it swayed through the other). It froze the game. Which rule caused the freeze is not proven; all were fixed together.
Fix: one wind node at the root (only if the file has wind shapes), the root carries the one BSXFlags and the main collision, inner wind nodes become plain NiNodes, collision scales baked into the hulls, duplicates removed. When combining meshes into one file, paste the shapes and their collision, not the other files' root, BSXFlags or wind node.
The Mossy Blender add-on's Check Against Game now reports BSXFlags or a wind node below the root, and collision without BSXFlags on the root.

title: AI-made tree leaves 'breathe' in the wind instead of blowing: replace them with flat leaf cards
content:
AI-made tree leaves 'breathe' in the wind instead of blowing: replace them with flat leaf cards
AI or photogrammetry trees often have leaves that are thin closed solids (a top skin, a bottom skin and edges), crumpled and made of several pieces, joined to the twigs. The Fallout 4 wind shader moves every vertex by its own alpha and times its sway by that alpha too, so such a leaf swells, twists and comes apart instead of swaying. Changing the wind painting does not fix it, and pressing the old leaves flat piece by piece tore them into spikes.
What works is what Bethesda does: flat leaf cards with an alpha-cut leaf texture, two-sided, one wind value per card. Remove the old leaf faces (thin parts whose surface points along one axis, above the root zone), then put a card where each group of leaves was: same facing as the old leaves, base at the nearest twig, random turn and size. One tree got 447 cards (3,576 triangles) using a bush's frond sheet and its material (two-sided, alpha test 128, Tree on) instead of 5,787 leaf triangles.
Cards need a texture with real alpha. A baked AI atlas (no alpha, scrambled pieces) cannot be used for cards; use a proper leaf or frond sheet.

title: Fallout 4 collision you walk through from some sides: convex hull written with too few planes (PyNifly packer)
content:
Fallout 4 collision you walk through from some sides: convex hull written with too few planes (PyNifly packer)
Symptom: a custom tree or plant stops the player from one side, but the player walks through it from the other sides. The collision looks right in Blender and NifSkope.
Cause: in a Fallout 4 convex hull (hknpConvexPolytopeShape) every face needs a plane. PyNifly's Havok packer (still in PyNifly 30.2.0) writes the size of the plane list as the VERTEX count, but it writes one plane per face. A hull made in Blender is all triangles, so it has about twice as many faces as vertices: a tree trunk hull had 126 faces but only 65 planes, so Havok only knew half of its sides. 18 of 373 hull-collision meshes in one set of mod folders had this.
Vanilla layout (all 1,195 vanilla convex hulls checked): vertex count a multiple of 4 (the last vertex repeated), plane count = face count rounded up to a multiple of 4, planes stored right after the vertices, faces right after the planes and padded to the same count, shape flags 0x0143.
Fix: rebuild the hull with that layout (same points, faces, radius and Havok material). The Mossy Blender add-on now writes hulls this way whenever it builds collision, and repairs hulls in exported files after every export ('collision hull planes rebuilt like vanilla'). Updating PyNifly alone does not fix it.

title: Fallout 4 tree wind like Bethesda's: the 3D wood stays still, only the leaf cards move (0 at the branch, 1 at the tip)
content:
Fallout 4 tree wind like Bethesda's: the 3D wood stays still, only the leaf cards move (0 at the branch, 1 at the tip)
Measured on the pre-war trees (Meshes\Landscape\Trees\Chargen: TreeMaplePreWar03Green, TreeElmForestPreWar01Green, TreeElmForestPreWar02Green, TreeElmFreePreWar01Green): the trunk and branches (the 3D wood) have vertex alpha 0 everywhere. All the movement is in the leaf clusters, and each one ramps from 0 where it meets the branch to 1.0 (255) at its tip. The thin twigs that carry the leaves are part of the flat leaf-card texture, not 3D geometry.
Symptom when this is not followed: 3D branches and twigs given wind 'breathe' (swell and shrink) instead of swaying, because the wind shader moves and times every vertex by its own alpha, and a thin tube with uneven alpha distorts.
Fix used on a custom tree with flat frond cards: wind 0 on the whole trunk shape (its material must still have Tree on, or alpha 0 becomes transparency), and each card ramped 0 at its base, 0.5 in the middle, 1.0 at the tip, so the card bends like a leaf.

AI-made tree or plant looks wet and plastic in Fallout 4: its specular map is far too strong

title: Collision for a cluster of big mushrooms in Fallout 4: one hull per stem and per cap, not one hull round the cluster
content:
Collision for a cluster of big mushrooms in Fallout 4: one hull per stem and per cap, not one hull round the cluster
A convex hull is shrink-wrap without dents: one hull round a mushroom cluster fills all the space between the mushrooms and under the caps, so the player bumps into empty air. Bethesda uses one hull for small fungi (FungusBrain, WastelandFungusStalk) and a mesh collision that follows the shape for its big fungal trees (BlastedForestFungalTree). Mesh collision written by PyNifly crashes the Creation Kit, so for a big cluster use one convex hull per stem (stopping a little below the cap, or the cap's underside flares it into a cone) and one per cap. A 12-mushroom cluster got 24 hulls; the player can walk between the mushrooms and under the big caps. Vanilla fungus hulls use the Havok material Grass.
The same mistake makes 'one giant wall' of plants: when several plants on a cliff or rock are exported as ONE piece (all plants sharing a material, or a piece named after a .bgsm), Collision wraps one hull round all of them and the player cannot walk between them. Measured on a Glowing Sea cliff: one hull 1,760 units wide round 6 spore plants and 48 small stalks, and a second one round 45 thin stalks. Fix: one hull per plant tall enough to block (there: 6 plants 350-510 tall, 17 stalks 250 tall or more), Grass material like every vanilla fungus hull, and no hull for small stalks. Check the hull's name against the material: that cliff's 'GSFungusSpore12' hull actually held GSFungusSpore7 plants. Since add-on 5.5.2+ (2026-11-14) Add Collision splits fungus, mushroom and spore meshes by itself; a model exported before that keeps its wall until its collision is made again.
Grass: of 110 vanilla grass meshes only 4 have collision (DLC04 GrassMoundHalves05-08): a low hull following the mound (about 66 units tall) that you walk up and over, Grass material. Normal grass has none, and Fallout 4 grass does not bend when you walk into it, so there is no 'sway' collision to add.

title: Giving an AI-made tree a proper bark texture in Blender: weld, unwrap, project a tiling bark
content:
Giving an AI-made tree a proper bark texture in Blender: weld, unwrap, project a tiling bark
1. An AI tree's texture atlas usually shares its space with the leaves and is a scrambled bake. A tree imported from a NIF is also cut apart at every old UV seam (one tree: 15,500 vertices in about 2,600 pieces), so every unwrap keeps those cuts. Weld first: join vertices on the same spot and drop loose vertices (that tree's trunk became one piece of 2,552 vertices).
2. Unwrap the welded mesh with an organic, fewest-islands unwrap. Measured on that trunk: 356 islands, 94% of the surface within 2x of the average texture detail. Cutting it by hand into trunk / branches / roots / crown collapsed a third of the surface, because AI trunks have hidden loops (branches that grow back in).
3. A single tiling bark image cannot be lined up by hand on hundreds of islands. Project it in 3D instead (box projection, blended, at a real-world tile size such as 120 game units = 1.7 m) and bake it into the UVs: the bark wraps continuously with no seams between islands. Make the normal map from the bark's brightness and keep the specular map low (vanilla pre-war bark: specular 14-16, smoothness 11-40 of 255).
4. Do not re-export the full tree NIF from Blender if it already has hand-checked collision: take only the new trunk shape into the good NIF.
In the Mossy Blender add-on: UV & Texture Kit > Fewest Islands (with Weld Import Cuts First, on by default), then UV & Texture Kit or Vegetation > Tree Tools > Project Tiling Texture onto UVs. It writes _d (BC7), _n and _s (BC5) DDS files to Downloads\FO4 Add-on Textures\Textures\<name>.

title: How much collision a Fallout 4 plant or bush gets: one hull per plant, none on the leaves
content:
How much collision a Fallout 4 plant or bush gets: one hull per plant, none on the leaves
Measured on all 195 vanilla Landscape\Plants NIFs (base game, Far Harbor, Nuka-World): 111 have collision, 84 have none, and no plant has more than 4 collision bodies; almost all have exactly 1. The leaves never get their own collision. Bushes and shrubs (56 vanilla NIFs): 43 have no collision at all, the other 13 have one simple hull, often just a box, round the woody core and smaller than the foliage, so the player brushes into the leaves before being stopped (deadshrubGS01: a 170-unit box inside a 400-unit-wide bush, Wood material; ChargenPrivetHedge01: Grass).
Symptom when this goes wrong: a bush with dozens of collision pieces, many smaller than 10 units, round single leaf clusters. Cause: a bush mesh is often one woody core plus many loose leaf clusters, and splitting collision 'one hull per separate piece' (meant for several plants merged into one object) gives every leaf cluster a hull. A Glowing Sea bush 211 units tall came out with 32 hulls.
Fix: keep one hull round the core (stems and low side shoots) and none on the leaves; for a bush, Wood like the Glowing Sea dead shrubs. The Mossy Blender add-on's Add Collision (after 5.5.2, 2026-11-15) now does this itself: a piece that sits up in the crown of a taller piece close by gets no hull, a low side shoot joins its plant's hull, pieces too small to block (under 48 units, or under a fifth of the tallest plant) get none, and separate plants keep one hull each. Measured with it: that bush 32 -> 1 hull, a cluster of 45 spore stalks 47 -> 20, a group of spore plants 61 -> 16; a mushroom cluster stays at one hull per stem and cap.

title: Little 3D parts breathe in the wind (pollen studs, antenna balls, curled stalks): one value per small part
content:
Little 3D parts breathe in the wind (pollen studs, antenna balls, curled stalks): one value per small part
Symptom: the plant sways fine, but small 3D parts on it - pollen studs on a flower, balls on the ends of antennas, short stalks - get bigger and smaller instead of swaying, and curved antennas bulge. Fallout 4's tree wind moves every vertex by its own vertex alpha, so any change of value INSIDE a small solid part stretches and squashes it. Measured on two Glowing Sea bushes: the 9-unit stalks under the pollen studs were painted 0 at the foot to 0.51 at the tip, so each stud rode the full sway while its foot stayed still; one antenna ball ran 0 to 0.49 inside a 10-unit sphere; curved antenna stalks painted along a straight line had different values on their inner and outer side.
Fix: a part too small to bend (under about 6% of the plant's size) gets ONE value, the wind of the bigger piece where it is attached, and parts that touch (a stud on its stalk) share that value; a curved stalk is painted along its own length (distance over the surface from its root), so each ring of it carries one value. Vanilla agrees: compact pieces sitting on a support carry one value (77%), equal to the support's (88%). On the two bushes the spread of wind between neighbouring vertices (within 4 units) on the fixed parts fell from 63 and 96 of 255 to 5 and 3 (95th percentile). The Mossy Blender add-on's Wind button does this since 2026-11-15; it was checked against Bethesda's own wind on 23 vanilla shapes (average difference 66.6 -> 66.3 of 255, no worse overall). To repair a plant whose wind you otherwise like, change only those parts, not a full repaint. Also check the root: a plant with collision needs BSXFlags 130 on its root like vanilla, or the game may ignore its collision.

title: New skin over a vanilla building: doors blocked after adding collision, and how to collide the skin without sealing them
content:
New skin over a vanilla building: doors blocked after adding collision, and how to collide the skin without sealing them
Symptom: a new outer mesh (a 'skin') was dropped over a vanilla building to give it a new look, keeping the inside, and after export you can no longer walk through the doors. Two things went wrong on a Glowing Sea shack (ShackMetalPrefabCompleteLg01 underneath): 1) Add Collision on the skin made ONE convex hull round the whole skin (1,500 units across). A convex hull has no openings, so it seals every door. 2) The vanilla building keeps its walls AND its c_NavCut boxes in ONE physics system: the building node uses body 0, the five NavCut nodes bodies 1-5. Re-exporting through PyNifly split every NavCut body into a physics system of its own (1 system became 6, even on a building only imported and exported again) and the export also changed the building's collision materials to Stone (wrong footstep and hit sounds on metal).
Fix that worked in game: keep the vanilla collision byte for byte (walls, door openings, NavCut bodies on their original body numbers, original materials) - a wall is one thin slab that stops you inside AND outside, so the 'outside' of the old building cannot be removed. Give the skin its own collision only where it sticks out past the old walls: many small convex hulls (about 110 units each) that follow the skin, never inside the building's outline and never in a clear zone in front of a doorway. Doorways are found from the building's own collision: gaps in its outline that are open at knee, waist and head height. Check afterwards that from just outside each doorway a person-sized path leads away at all three heights. Result: 149 skin hulls (Organic material) following the skin within 3.5 units (median), all three outside doors clear; confirmed working in game. Bigger pieces (160 units, 73 hulls) are lighter but leave twice as many invisible bumps more than 20 units out (9% vs 4%). The add-on now does all of this itself: Generate Collision on a skin over a building (also in Mesh Helpers > Skin Builder). Where the skin bends round a corner next to a doorway, the hulls there are split smaller so none reaches into the clear zone (a three-copy skin on the same shack: 297 hulls, doors clear).

title: Putting an AI-made skin (Meshy) over a Fallout 4 building: the Skin Builder workflow, step by step
content:
Putting an AI-made skin (Meshy) over a Fallout 4 building: the Skin Builder workflow, step by step
Who does what: the modder makes the shape, the add-on does the rest. 1) Shape (by hand in Blender): import the building with the add-on, import the AI model (Meshy .glb), place as many copies as needed to cover the building (a large shack took three, made wider and longer), reduce them with Decimate (about 21,000 triangles for three copies looked right; lower started to look bad), and delete the parts that show inside the building. Do NOT re-unwrap or re-texture the reduced skin: its UVs still point into the original's texture and that is what the bake uses. Save the .blend. 2) Textures: Fallout 4 panel > Mesh Helpers > Skin Builder (AI skin over a building) > select the skin > pick the original model > Bake Original onto My Remesh (a few minutes). It writes 4K _d, _n, _s and _g DDS textures and a .BGSM (two-sided, glow map on the eyes at 0.8, wet leaf template) and gives the skin a material pointing at them. 3) Collision: Generate Collision on the skin. Over a building it makes small hulls (about 110 units) only outside the building's walls, keeps a clear zone in front of every doorway, and puts the building's own collision back exactly on export. 4) Check Doors: walks a person-sized body out of every doorway at knee, waist and head height against all collision. 5) Copy the Materials and Textures into the mod BEFORE exporting the NIF: the export writes a plain material for any .BGSM it cannot find, which loses the glow and textures. After updating the add-on, restart Blender: a Blender left open keeps running the old code (a shack exported that way got one hull round the whole skin and its door was blocked). Results on a Glowing Sea shack: textures matched the approved in-game look, 97 skin hulls, building collision identical to vanilla, all three doors clear; in game: 'it came out amazing'.

title: How Bake Original onto My Remesh works, and why the textures of a reduced AI model looked wrong before
content:
How Bake Original onto My Remesh works, and why the textures of a reduced AI model looked wrong before
Reducing a 3-million-face AI model to a game-ready size and keeping its own texture stretches the texture over the bigger triangles, so it no longer looks like the original. The fix is to bake the full original onto the reduced mesh. The reduced skin still carries the original's UVs, so every vertex says which point of the original it came from; each separate copy in the skin (found as a connected piece; small loose bits go with the nearest copy) is lined up with the full original from those points by a fitted move/turn/stretch that ignores wrong matches (three copies lined up within 0.12-0.13% of their size, 94-97% of points agreeing). Each copy is baked alone, with only its own lined-up original present: baked together, overlapping copies steal each other's texture. Baked per copy: colour, tangent-space normal (DirectX, green flipped, as Fallout 4), roughness and coverage, then merged by coverage because the copies share one texture layout. Shine (_s, red = green) is levelled to the wet, living look of Materializer maps (10% at 0.28, 90% at 0.79, mean about 0.52). Glow (_g) is only bright warm eye-sized spots (more than 3000 texels at 4K) counted on texture that is really used - counted on the filled gaps, pale thorn tips looked eye-sized and glowed. Colour 'As approved' reproduces the approved look (Blender's AgX on save: mid-tones about 5% darker, highlights softer); 'Exact original colours' keeps the AI model's colours. Limits: the copies share one bump map, so the fine bump detail fits each copy within a few levels, not exactly; a skin that was re-unwrapped or sculpted after reducing cannot be lined up and the button says so.

title: Auto-Repair reports thousands of loose vertices on every click - the count was wrong, nothing is loose
content:
Auto-Repair reports thousands of loose vertices on every click - the count was wrong, nothing is loose
Old Auto-Repair counted 'loose vertices' from data that is out of date while Blender is in Edit Mode, so it reported every vertex as loose (a skin with none loose: 'removed 43100 loose vertices', then 'removed 13270' on the next click). Fixed: Auto-Repair now reports the real number of loose vertices removed and how many seam vertices were joined.

title: Getting a building that is not a prefab out of the game to put a skin over it (example: Mother Isolde's house, Crater of Atom)
content:
Getting a building that is not a prefab out of the game to put a skin over it (example: Mother Isolde's house, Crater of Atom)
Many buildings are not one NIF but dozens of pieces placed in the world (Mother Isolde's house at the Crater of Atom is 49 vanilla shack pieces in Fallout4.esm). To find the right ones: an NPC's AI packages point at markers where they sleep, pray or sandbox - Isolde's sleep marker (z 8115, upstairs) and prayer spot are both inside the same building, while her placed position is out on the walkway. Read every placed reference near those markers, group the pieces that touch (leaving out walkway bridges), and assemble them in Blender from the unpacked meshes with each reference's position, rotation and scale. Many pieces are flipped (rotation 180 deg on X), so the rotations must be applied exactly; furniture, crates and clutter stay separate in the world. For skinning, a reference .blend of the house is enough: same metre scale as the add-on's imports, pieces marked as references (never exported), the Blender origin set to one game position (here X -102298.72, Y -116850.11, Z 7842.79). The finished skin is exported on its own and placed in the Creation Kit at that position with rotation 0 and scale 1, over the untouched original house; collision goes on the skin only.

title: Collision doubled (2 bodies became 4) after re-exporting a NIF from Blender
content:
Collision doubled (2 bodies became 4) after re-exporting a NIF from Blender
Collision that PyNifly imports from a NIF arrives as plain meshes named bhkPhysicsSystem... carrying only PyNifly's own marker. The add-on's scene export used to treat them as visible meshes: it 'prepared' them (the export then warned that bhkPhysicsSystem had no UV map and got a placeholder unwrap) and looked for each one's collision; with exactly two such objects in a file each found the other, so both were attached again next to the copies PyNifly writes itself. Seen on a fungus tree: 2 collision bodies came back as 4 and one existing hull was changed. Fixed in the add-on: imported collision stays selected and scaled (PyNifly still writes it) but is no longer prepared or attached twice; re-exporting the same tree now gives its 2 bodies at their original sizes (only float rounding of about a thousandth of a unit). How to spot an old bad export: more physics systems in the NIF than before, extra nodes named bhkPhysicsSystem..._Collision, or the export message 'added next to the 2 collision(s) the file already had'.

title: Retextured vanilla plant: pieces come apart in the wind -> copy the vanilla wind back
content:
Retextured vanilla plant: pieces come apart in the wind -> copy the vanilla wind back
If a plant is a retexture of a vanilla mesh (same vertex count and positions as a vanilla NIF, for example Green_Bush02 = Far Harbor DLC04 Alder_Bush02), do not run a wind generator on it. Bethesda's wind keeps the joints of the cards low and only the outer ends swing, so the bush holds together; a copy with wind 1.0 (255) on every vertex makes every card swing fully on its own and the pieces visibly separate. Fix: copy the vanilla vertex-colour alpha back vertex by vertex (only the alpha byte; texture, material and LOD sizes stay). Re-exporting a BSMeshLODTriShape from Blender reorders its vertices, which can upset its distance detail levels, so patch the original file instead of re-exporting it.

title: Fallout 4 wind on 3D parts: what stays still and what may move (all vanilla wind NIFs measured)
content:
Fallout 4 wind on 3D parts: what stays still and what may move (all vanilla wind NIFs measured)
Measured on all 325 vanilla NIFs with a wind root (BSLeafAnimNode), 35,912 pieces. 3D parts (closed, or a tube/blob even if open at the base) are still in 89% of cases: trunks, branches, stalks, bulbs. Flat parts (leaf cards, fronds, strips) move: 0 where they touch their parent, about 0.5 at the tip, 1.0 when they hang off a solid trunk. The few 3D parts that move are kelp-like stalks: 0 at the base rising smoothly to only 0.09-0.24 at the top, with the same value all the way round the stalk at each height, so the stalk bends as one piece. 3D parts 'breathe' (swell and shrink) when values differ around the same part (a ramp across a bulb, nubs at different values from the surface under them). Used on custom plants: thin 3D pollen stalks 0 -> 0.24 along their centreline (moved without breathing in game), bulb and nubs still, side branches still with the leaves hanging from them ramped 0 -> 1.

title: Holes appear only once the texture is on (model is closed, see-through gaps along the texture's painted edges)
content:
Holes appear only once the texture is on (model is closed, see-through gaps along the texture's painted edges)
Cause: the model's UV islands reach a little past the painted area of the diffuse texture. Outside the painted area the texture's alpha is 0 (and the colour is often black), so the viewport shows those faces as holes; in the game they are cut away if the material has alpha test on, or show dark/odd patches if it is off. Check: overlay the UV layout on the texture's alpha channel; faces sitting on black alpha are the holes (a fungus pod: 42 of 1,821 faces, along three island edges). Fix that keeps the painting: bleed the painted colours outward into the blank area (nearest painted colour, about 200 texels at 4K) and make those texels opaque, in the diffuse and the normal map, then save in the same format (BC7 for _d, BC5 with a DX10 header for _n). Painted texels stay byte-identical. Moving the UVs inward also works but changes the look.

title: Roots block the path: collision makes a wall over roots that lie on the ground and curl up at the end
content:
Roots block the path: collision makes a wall over roots that lie on the ground and curl up at the end
Cause: each root got one convex hull. A hull is the tightest shape with no dents, so a root that lies on the ground and curls up at its tip becomes a tall slanted wedge from the trunk out to the raised tip, and the player cannot step over the root. Fix: shorter hulls along each root, so each part hugs the root. The Blender add-on's Add Collision now does this itself (since 2026-11-17): a long piece lying mostly flat is cut across its length when two halves need clearly less hull than the whole (a curl or arch), up to 8 parts per root; straight roots and upright stalks keep one hull. Measured on two fungus trees: widest ground hull 9.2-9.7 m down to 3.6-5.6 m, tallest root hull 245-275 down to 173-177 units.

title: Make 3D plant parts sway without breathing: a looping Idle animation instead of wind
content:
Make 3D plant parts sway without breathing: a looping Idle animation instead of wind
Fallout 4's tree wind (vertex alpha + the Tree_Anim shader flag) moves every vertex on its own, so fat 3D parts (bulbs, thick branches, pollen nubs) swell and shrink - they 'breathe' instead of blowing. The way vanilla moves solid parts on a static model is a rigid node animation that plays by itself: the root gets a NiControllerManager with one NiControllerSequence named "Idle", cycle type LOOP, frequency 1.0; a NiMultiTargetTransformController drives one NiTransformInterpolator + NiTransformData (rotation keys) per animated node; a NiTextKeyExtraData holds the 'start' and 'end' keys; a NiDefaultAVObjectPalette lists the named nodes; and BSXFlags has bit 0 (Animated) set. Vanilla examples placed as plain STAT that play on their own: street banners (BannerStreetConcord01 7.5 s, StreetLampBanner02 13 s), BOSRadarDish (12 s), the pre-war prop-wash trees CG_PrewarTreesPropWash01/02 (9 s, BSLeafAnimNode root).
How it was done on a custom glowing bush: split the mesh into pieces (the centre bulb, and each branch with the pollen nubs that sit on it), put each piece under its own NiNode whose origin is the piece's pivot (where the branch meets the bulb, the bulb's base), with the vertices moved so they are relative to that pivot; turn the wind off (vertex alpha 0) so the shader adds no swell on top; give each node a gentle rotation loop (bulb about 1.5 degrees, branches about 4 degrees, a main sway toward one wind direction plus a smaller second wave, a phase offset per piece so they do not move in step, first and last key equal so the loop is seamless; 6 s loop, keys every 0.2 s). Each piece swings rigidly, so nothing can breathe, and the nubs move with their branch. Tested in game by the mod author: it works and looks better than the wind animation did. The block order matters - see the entry on the Creation Kit crash 'Sequence already has an owner'.

title: Creation Kit crashes when you click an animated NIF: 'Error adding sequence: Sequence already has an owner'
content:
Creation Kit crashes when you click an animated NIF: 'Error adding sequence: Sequence already has an owner'
Symptom: the CK crashes the moment you select or preview a model that has its own animation (a NiControllerManager with an Idle or other sequence). The CKPE crash log (Fallout 4\Logs\CKPE\Crashes\*.zip, file CreationKitPlatformExtendedCrash.log) shows 'Error adding sequence: Sequence already has an owner.' and then an access violation with a NiControllerManager in the registers and the STAT's name next to it. Cause: block order inside the NIF. The game and CK set up the blocks in the order they are stored; when a NiControllerSequence is stored BEFORE its NiControllerManager, the sequence is already owned when the manager tries to add it, the add fails, and the manager then reads an empty slot. Vanilla always stores the manager first: in all 1,623 vanilla NIFs with a NiControllerManager, 6,475 of 6,475 sequences come after their manager. Vanilla order: root node, its extra data (BSXFlags), NiControllerManager, NiMultiTargetTransformController, NiControllerSequence, then each NiTransformInterpolator with its NiTransformData, NiTextKeyExtraData, NiDefaultAVObjectPalette, then the nodes and shapes. Fix: reorder the blocks (and renumber every link) so the manager comes before its sequences - nothing else needs to change. This mostly happens with hand-built or script-built animated NIFs.
